To ensure students feel happy and safe from day one, we offer a carefully planned transition programme, including induction days, taster lessons, and primary school visits from our staff.

Our inclusive and caring environment ensures that every student feels valued and supported, while our ambitious, future-focused curriculum equips them with the knowledge and skills needed for excellence in the modern world.
We empower our students to realise their full potential, celebrate the diversity that strengthens our community, and foster a culture of respect, responsibility and strong relationships.

At the heart of its work is the mission of Educating for Life, ensuring every student receives an outstanding education that prepares them for the future, underpinned by the vision of achieving excellence for all with no excuses.

pageCache.pageTitle: Norbury High School for Girls - Student Wins Shakespeare's Globe Art Competition
pageCache.text:
Student Wins Shakespeare's Globe Art Competition
Year 8 student's winning entry will be displayed to over 30,000 students
Year 8 student Hadeeqa Islam has won a prestigious national art competition organised by Shakespeare's Globe.
The brief was to design graffiti for the 2026 Playing Shakespeare with Deutsche Bank production of Romeo and Juliet based around one or two words from the play.
Hadeeqa’s electric design (below) was selected by Natalie Pryce, the production’s Olivier Award-winning designer, to form part of the set. It is now expected to be viewed by over 30,000 theatregoers.
Playing Shakespeare with Deutsche Bank: Romeo and Juliet is a fast-paced, 90-minute, contemporary staging created especially for young people. It will be performed at Shakespeare's Globe between 5th March and 12th April 2026 with dedicated school performances taking place from 26th February to 25th March 2026.

pageCache.pageTitle: Norbury High School for Girls - Choirs Win Festival Music Awards
pageCache.text:
Choirs Win Festival Music Awards
Celeste and the Show Choir took first prize in their respective categories
On Saturday 28th February, our school choirs competed in the Coulsdon and Purley Festival, a long-established local music and arts festival that celebrates performers of all ages and provides a platform for emerging talent.
Our Show Choir came first with honours in the 12-18 choirs category while Celeste came first with honours in the vocal ensemble category. To cap off an excellent evening for Norbury High School for Girls, Celeste were awarded The Eric Thiman Cup for best youth vocal ensemble.
Celeste collected the Eric Thiman trophy at Coulsdon and Purley Festival's celebration concert and prize-giving event at Wilson’s School on Saturday 25th April. They were joined by Arian Edwards, a Norbury High alumnus, who was awarded the Marion Lea Cup for British song, 15–18 years.
These fantastic achievements are a testament to the talent and dedication of our students, past and present, and the unceasing support and hard work of Ms Stevens, our choir leader.

Welcome to our sixth form course guides and Find Out More hub. This is your first or next step in researching and considering the subjects you might wish to study in year 12.

Each department has prepared a Find Out More card that links to course guides and further info. These are designed to help you:

Start by browsing the Find Out More cards for the A level or level 3 subjects that interest you. Then, use them as a way to ‘test-drive’ your options, read, research and reflect. This is your chance to discover what excites you, what challenges you and learn which subjects feel right for your next step.

pageCache.pageTitle: Norbury High School for Girls - ASRA Runners Take Part in Black to the Trails
pageCache.text:
ASRA Runners Take Part in Black to the Trails
Students challenge themselves in UK’s most ethnically diverse trail running event
Students from the ASRA run club recently took part in the Black to the Trails Race, the UK’s most ethnically diverse trail running event.
In preparation for the event, which took place on Sunday 10th May on the National Trust's Dunstable Downs and Whipsnade Estate, 12 students successfully completed a six-week training programme with ASRA. Before race day, each was provided with limited-edition ASRA x On kit including a windbreaker, top, bottoms and trainers.
On the day, 10 students completed their very first 5K race in under 40 minutes — an incredible achievement. A special mention goes to Elaina R and Safia B, who both completed the race in under 30 minutes. The remaining two students completed their first ever 1K race in under 8 minutes.
The Black to the Trails event, which is described as 'A Carnival of Trail Running', also featured kite flying, face painting, great food and plenty of memorable moments. All students received medals and goodie bags to celebrate their achievements.
See our picture gallery for more images.

pageCache.pageTitle: Norbury High School for Girls - Partnerships
pageCache.text:
Partnerships
The school has forged a number of mutually beneficial partnerships over the years. Among the organisations we are affiliated with are Goldsmiths, the University of Sussex, St Mary's University and UCL Institute of Education, where many of our student teachers are trained. The college has been awarded Specialist Partner (Initial Teacher Training) status by UCL Institute of Education.
We share expertise and resources with Kensington Avenue Primary School, a fellow academy overseen by Wandle Learning Trust. We also maintain close contact with a further six primaries - Norbury Manor Primary School, Downsview Primary School, Kingsley Primary School, Winterbourne Girls Junior School, Elmwood Junior School and Purley Oaks Primary School.
Information about our Discovery Workshops, aimed at key stage 2 pupils from local primary schools with whom we collaborate, please use the link on the right-hand side of this page.
Our partnership with Olive Dining, provider of the school's catering services, has enabled Norbury High - the first secondary school in Croydon to be awarded the Healthy Schools London Silver Award - to maintain our high standards.

pageCache.pageTitle: Norbury High School for Girls - Students Celebrate on GCSE Results Day
pageCache.text:
Students Celebrate on GCSE Results Day
School's Progress 8 score is in the Well Above Average range
Students at Norbury High were celebrating on GCSE results day after achieving more top grades (9-7) this year than last year across six subjects: English language, Spanish, psychology, sociology, PE and art and design.
Among those celebrating were Sofia Noorzad, who received six grade 9s and three grade 8s; Aizza Shahid (four 9s and three 8s); Palakshi Sharma (three 9s and four 8s); and Hadia Ahmadi (one 9 and eight 8s).
The school also achieved a Progress 8 measurement of +0.59 which would ordinarily* have placed it in the WELL ABOVE AVERAGE banding.
In English there was another fantastic Progress 8 figure of +1.03 reported (an improvement on last year's +0.87 score). The Progress 8 figure for maths also gained ground, with the school delivering its best progress results in mathematics since the Covid-19 pandemic.
Mrs Hayden, Headteacher, said: “We are immensely proud of our year 11 students. The improvement in our Progress 8 figure to +0.59 (well above average) is a significant achievement despite not being formally recognised externally this year*.
“We are especially pleased with the excellent progress in English, the continued improvements in maths and the very strong performance across our EBacc subjects.
"These results reflect the hard work and resilience of our students, alongside the dedication of our staff and the support of families."
* The government has stated "It will not be possible to calculate Progress 8 for academic years 2024 to 2025 and 2025 to 2026 due to gaps in the baseline caused by COVID-19 disruption."
